item.rapidinsulinpendsc: A 100ml syringe offering precise control over dosage. Injects 2ml on use. The cartridge inside says to take with food.
item.rapidinsulindsc: A 100ml vial. Doesn't seem like you could drink from it. The label says to take with food.
item.longinsulinpendsc: A 100ml syringe offering precise control over dosage. Injects 10ml on use. The cartridge inside says to take once a "day".
item.longinsulindsc: A 100ml vial. Doesn't seem like you could drink from it. The label says to take regularly.
item.glucagondsc: A 100ml syringe that can inject fluid intramuscularly. It says to give all of it.
item.insulinpumpdsc: While worn, injects at a fixed rate from a 100ml reservoir. Helps keep your blood glucose stable when used with rapid-acting insulin. Use while wearing to inject 2ml manually for food.
item.smartinsulinpumpdsc: While worn, injects dynamically from a 100ml reservoir in response to your blood glucose level, keeping it stable when used with rapid-acting insulin. Use while wearing to inject 2ml manually for food.
item.glucosemeterdsc: A device that checks the amount of glucose in a drop of blood. Some of the testing strips it uses are taped to the back, along with a lancet. Use on your paw to prick your finger and check your blood glucose.

moodle.honeymoondsc: Often, shortly after type 1 diabetes is diagnosed and treatment started, the pancreas regains some function for a short time. It seems there's hope for you after all; insulin needs greatly reduced.
moodle.ketoacidosis1dsc: Acidic bodies are building up in your blood. Are you taking enough insulin?
moodle.ketoacidosis2dsc: You feel ill. Ketones beginning to lower your blood pH. Insulin is less effective; take more than usual.
moodle.ketoacidosis3dsc: Horribly sick and confused. You have a weird taste in your mouth and your blood is highly acidic. You will die without insulin.
moodle.ketoacidosis4dsc: Your blood has the pH of lemon juice. Your cells are dying off: coma and brain death imminent.
moodle.hypoglycemia1dsc: Something's off. Lay off the insulin and try to eat some sugar.
moodle.hypoglycemia2dsc: Weak, shaky, and sweaty. Avoid insulin and eat something sweet to increase your blood glucose.
moodle.hypoglycemia3dsc: Can't think... Burning up... In urgent need of sugar or glucagon.
moodle.hypoglycemia4dsc: Neurons non-functional due to a lack of glucose. If you don't recover soon, organs will start failing.
moodle.hyperglycemia1dsc: Your blood glucose is over target. Correct with some insulin.
moodle.hyperglycemia2dsc: Thirstier than normal. Correct your blood glucose with insulin.
moodle.hyperglycemia3dsc: Your blood sugar is way too high. Quickly becoming dehydrated. Take plenty of insulin and watch for ketones.
moodle.hyperglycemia4dsc: Syrup running through your veins, you're drying out from the inside...

other.hpbloodsugardsc: The amount of sugar in your blood. Below 4.0 is too little and above 10.0 is too much. You'll pass out if it gets too low.
other.hpbloodsugarmgdldsc: The amount of sugar in your blood. Below 70 is too little and above 180 is too much. You'll pass out if it gets too low.
other.hpketonesdsc: Presence of acidic ketone bodies, kept at bay by insulin. Should be as low as possible. 0.6 mmol/l or higher is problematic.
other.hpinsulinsensdsc: The extent to which insulin affects blood glucose. The base value is 1.0, where 1ml will reduce it by 2.0 mmol/l. Only visible by cheating.
other.rapidinsulindsc: A hormone that decreases blood glucose quickly when injected. Lowers glucose by about 2.0 mmol/l per ml. Less effective when unwell.
other.rapidinsulinmgdldsc: A hormone that decreases blood glucose quickly when injected. Lowers glucose by about 36 mg/dl per ml. Less effective when unwell.
other.longinsulindsc: A hormone that slowly decreases blood glucose over a long time when injected. Counteracts the natural increase of glucose and ketones. Less effective when unwell.
other.metformindsc: An oral medication that improves insulin sensitivity. Can help keep blood glucose stable.
other.glucagondsc: The counterpart to insulin, a hormone that increases blood glucose quickly when injected. Could prove useful in an emergency.
other.sweeturinedsc: Sweetened lemon-flavored drink. Tasty, though it smells a bit off.
other.runsetglycogenolysisratedsc: The rate at which your blood glucose rises naturally.
other.runsetpancreaseffectdsc: The amount of residual effect your pancreas has towards stabilizing your blood glucose.
other.runseticrdsc: How many grams of carbohydrate will be offset by 1ml of insulin. A higher number means carbs will increase your blood glucose less.
other.runsetisfdsc: The amount by which 1ml of insulin will decrease your blood glucose. A higher number means insulin is more effective.
other.runsethypotimescaledsc: The speed the blood sugar simulation (not the whole game) runs at while you are hypoglycemic.
other.glucoseMeterMinigameGuide: Apply blood to the end of the test strip, then wait for the reading.
